title: IBA and Framatome form Ekalia for At-211 production
summary: On Friday, Framatome and Ion Beam Applications announced the next step in their plan to advance the industrial-scale production of astatine-211 in Europe and the United States. The partners have formed a jointly owned company, Ekalia, through which they will deploy a network of At-211 production sites close to customers. According to IBA, the first production site is planned in Nantes, France, and Ekalia expects to invest €30 million (about $33.6 million) in it. The permit application has been submitted, the start of construction is anticipated in early 2027, and the site is expected to become operational in 2028. A second pilot site is planned in the United States, though the location and timing have yet to be confirmed.

title: Centrus Announces $116 Million Acquisition Of Centrifuge Component Supplier Westerman
summary: US nuclear fuel company Centrus Energy has acquired Westerman Holdings, a major supplier of components for its uranium enrichment centrifuges, for about $116m (€103m), a statement said. Centrus said the acquisition was financed through about $95m in cash and $21m in equity.

title: IAEA publishes report on isotope tracing for water pollution monitoring
summary: After a four-year coordinated research project involving 14 countries to develop and test new isotope-based methods for tracing nitrate pollution in river and groundwater systems led by the International Atomic Energy Agency, a report has been published describing the outcomes. The countries that participated in the study were Argentina, Australia, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Ecuador, Finland, France, Greece, Italy, Malaysia, Nigeria, Pakistan, Spain, and Ukraine.

title: Slovakia’s Mochovce-4 Nuclear Power Plant Connected To Grid For First Time
summary: The Mochovce-4 nuclear power plant in Slovakia has been connected to the national electricity grid for the first time, marking a major milestone in the commissioning of the VVER-440 reactor unit. Slovak owner Slovenské Elektrárne said the first of the unit’s two turbine generators was synchronised with the grid at 20:41 local time on 15 October and began supplying electricity.

title: Browns Ferry and the fight against eelgrass
summary: Opportunities to improve maintenance efficiency can arise unexpectedly at nuclear power plants. At Browns Ferry in Athens, Ala., one opportunity arose when an unexpected surge of nonnative eelgrass in the Tennessee River clogged the cooling water intake, prompting the shutdown of two reactors and the derating of a third to about 78 percent power. Power plant engineers said the single surge reportedly cost the Tennessee Valley Authority about $15 million–$20 million in revenue. A 2026 report from the International Atomic Energy Agency said the same incident resulted in a production loss of roughly 0.5 terawatt-hours.
